label: C · Work in orbit
prompt: Create a high fidelity desktop WEBSITE UI MOCKUP, 1440x1100 canvas, for software developer Otniel Rahadiyan Sumantri, aimed at hiring recruiters. This is a designed web interface, not a poster, no device frame. Visual world: a contemporary astronomical observatory and precise solar system atlas. Warm ivory #F5F3EB background, deep ink navy #182534 text, solar orange #D85B2B accent, fine grey-blue orbital rules. Elegant distinctive modern grotesk typography with exceptionally strong hierarchy, NO serif or italics, no neon, no purple gradients, no glassmorphism, no rounded card grid. Accurate legible UI text. Header: small orbit symbol and 'otniel.' on left, 'Work', 'About', 'Contact' on right. Preserve the full name in readable text. Headline 'Software developer. Curious by nature.' Supporting copy 'Hi, I’m Otniel Rahadiyan Sumantri. I build software with care and explore what’s possible.' Buttons 'Explore my work' and 'About me'. Render an exceptionally crafted geometrical solar system diagram with a bright orange Sun, fine ellipses, flat colored planetary spheres, Earth with blue/green and Saturn with rings, small labels 'SUN', 'EARTH', 'SATURN'; accurate atlas-like geometry, circles, no cartoon faces. Lower section must show heading 'Selected work' and visibly marked 'Project placeholders — replace with your real work', with two tasteful bespoke developer project preview thumbnails, no invented metrics, clients, employment claims or fake links. Every region supports quick evaluation by a recruiter. Spacious refined professional design. Composition C: Project-led portfolio composition. Top left a large but compact headline and intro taking 60 percent width, right small solar system diagram taking 40 percent, buttons under intro. Hero finishes at approximately 480px. Below, a very prominent Selected work section showing TWO large bespoke illustrative project previews side by side with readable sample labels 'Project one' and 'Project two' and explicit placeholder disclosure. One preview shows a tasteful code editor interface, the other a refined astronomy application interface, clearly illustrative. Solar system imagery visually ties them together through tiny planet markers. The strongest screen area is project evidence, not decoration. Structured editorial composition and exceptional recruiter scanability.
